neighbours.label: the organism that breaks down or consumes material ('broken down by microbes', 'fed to pigs', 'eaten by')
fire: In the compost heap, the peelings are gradually broken down by bacteria and fungi.
Unlike paper, most plastics are never broken down by microorganisms in the soil.
On the smallholding, leftover bread is fed to the goats and hens.
The dead whale on the seabed is slowly eaten by hagfish and crabs.
In wetlands, the sewage is broken down by microbes living on the reeds.
Spent grain from the brewery is fed to cattle on nearby farms.
Fallen fruit in the orchard is soon broken down by insects and moulds.
Each night the scraps from the kitchen are fed to the worms in the bin.
quiet: In the compost heap, the peelings are gradually turned with a garden fork.
Unlike paper, most plastics are collected separately by the council.
On the smallholding, leftover bread is given to the neighbours on Sunday.
The dead whale on the seabed was filmed by a remote camera last spring.
In wetlands, the sewage project was approved by the regional council.
Spent grain from the brewery is sold to bakers in nearby towns.
Fallen fruit in the orchard is soon collected by the pickers and sold.
Each night the scraps from the kitchen are carried to the bin by the porter.

notes: Card: peaks ' by' x8, ' to' (fed to worms, given as food to organisms), 'decomposing', 'eaten by', 'through' (digest). The + pole is the transformation verb (break down, degrade). Probe: 'broken down into soil by fungi and bacteria' 1.41, 'not broken down by microbes' 0.78, 'feeds its vegetable scraps to pigs' 0.53, 'eaten by an owl' 0.34, bacteria digest sludge 0.27. Bureaucratic 'written by', 'given to', 'approved by' 0.00-0.08. Near misses keep the same scene and a by/to phrase but have no organism consuming the material.
